still_true: Wegovy's US list price is still $1,349 a month on the box, and almost nobody pays it.
The FDA has still approved no generic semaglutide or tirzepatide in the US. Generic liraglutide is still the only generic incretin on the US market, and exclusivity still runs to roughly 2031–32.
The TrumpRx cash channel still operates, and oral Wegovy starting doses still cost $149 a month there.
Novo Nordisk and Eli Lilly are still the only sellers of branded incretins in the US. Lilly still leads on efficacy, with tirzepatide at about 22% body-weight loss.

The 503B compounding exclusion finalised in 2026 still stands, the suicidal-ideation warning is still off the labels, the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge pilot has not been revived, and Illinois's ban on adherence-conditioned premiums is still in force.

population.note: FICTIONAL. Arithmetic: 31.0% ever-used − 24.4% current = 6.6% of adults who used and are off now. 44% of 31.0 = 13.6 points have cycled. About 11.6 points are current users on at least a second course (~48% of current users), and about 2.0 points are cyclers who are off again. That fits roughly one-third persistence at one year and 36–47% restarting within a year, made higher by habitual drug holidays. 24.4% of ~267M adults ≈ 65M current users. FICTIONAL payer mix: commercial ~31% (~20M, of whom ~4M are in adherence-verified tracks), Medicare ~15% (~10M: diabetes, CV, CKD and OSA codes plus ~1.6M on the tirzepatide dementia route), Medicaid ~7% (~4.5M), legitimate cash (TrumpRx/direct) ~33% (~21.5M), imported or counterfeit ~14% (~9M). Total 20+10+4.5+21.5+9 = 65M. Coverage structure did not change. Growth came from cash orals at lower maintenance prices (+7.5M), the gray-market flood (+6M), the dementia route (+~1.5M Medicare) and the new addiction label. The bottom third rose most (11→19%), almost entirely through mail-order vials and cash starting doses. Adult obesity is ~33.0%. About 21% of adults have obesity and have never used a drug, concentrated among the uninsured, Medicaid enrollees in non-covering states and rural older adults. Under-18 use (1.3%) is mostly ages 12–17 on orals. About 1 in 4 upper-income adolescents with severe obesity is on a drug, and a gray-market pediatric fringe of parents dosing teens from vials is being reported by poison centres. Off-drug adults (6.6%) are mostly GI quitters, people priced out, and older adults stopped on bone advice.

access.public_coverage: No structural change. Medicare Part D covers incretins only under diabetes, CV, CKD and OSA codes, plus the tirzepatide dementia-risk indication under prior authorisation. Dementia-route arithmetic: ~1.6M beneficiaries × ~$260 net/month × 12 ≈ $5.0B a year in 2030. The weight-only Medicare benefit remains barred. Medicaid: 9 states still opted in at the $245 rate, the same as end-2028; two of them make continued coverage conditional on adherence and BMI. Fewer than a quarter of Medicaid adults with obesity have a covered route.
access.generic_rest_of_world: Indian generic semaglutide costs $5–35/month across 80+ brands, and Chinese generic tirzepatide analogues are now exported in volume. Generics are sold in ~175 countries. Canada's generics are CAD 60–95. India and China supply most of the world's incretin volume.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Managed decline: the Jan 2029 TrumpRx/manufacturer round cut maintenance oral prices from $299 to $199–249, and injectables in the cash channel to $249–349. Starting oral doses stay at $149. PBM-negotiated commercial net prices fell ~12%. Brands hold $149–349 and coverage still rations access. Employer coverage is flat at 43%, and another ~10% cover only through monitored metabolic tracks. Orals are ~65% of new starts and ~50% of all users. The gray market is about 9M users: mail-order Indian and Chinese vials at $25–90/month, counterfeit pens, and 'research peptide' tirzepatide from Chinese websites. Personal-importation enforcement is still weak despite CBP seizures, which rose about fourfold.

on_market_classes: GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill 25 mg; Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: adolescent obesity 12+ (semaglutide incl. Wegovy pill, liraglutide)
reduction of risk of all-cause dementia in adults with obesity and established CVD (tirzepatide, 2028; confirmatory trial ongoing)
alcohol use disorder and gambling disorder in adults (oral semaglutide, Apr 2030; first incretin 'addictive disorders' label)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: compulsive shopping, compulsive sexual behaviour and 'screen compulsion', prescribed via telehealth on the back of the gambling label
dementia-prevention use by people without CVD, cash-paid on orals
shift-worker and trucker alcohol reduction encouraged by employers
drugs.pipeline_note: No new class reached the US market in 2029–30. Retatrutide got a complete response letter in Mar 2029 over dysesthesia and discontinuation imbalances; Lilly resubmitted with a lower-dose arm in Feb 2030 and expects a decision in 2031. Survodutide's review was extended after a major amendment on liver-enzyme and heart-rate data. It was approved in the EU in mid-2030; the US decision is due 2031. Amycretin was filed in Sep 2029, so a decision can come no earlier than late 2030, and FDA set a 2031 goal date. MariTide and bimagrumab-type adjuncts are not on the market; MariTide is in phase 3 and bimagrumab in phase 3 combination trials. The compulsion driver came through an existing product in a new indication. Novo filed an sNDA for oral semaglutide in alcohol use disorder and gambling disorder in Feb 2029, using its AUD phase 3 and a 26-week gambling-disorder phase 3 (~11 fewer gambling days a month vs ~6 on placebo). Approval came Apr 2030. Global incretin market ~$140B (2030 est.). US net prices are falling slowly while volume rises.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation. A new pattern: ER visits for severe vomiting and dehydration when users restart at full maintenance dose after a drug holiday instead of re-titrating.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled. A 2029 label update added re-titration instructions after missed doses of more than 2 weeks (injectables) or 5 days (orals).

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Elevated with rapid weight loss; unchanged.
No causal confirmation; absolute risk low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; the MDL global settlement was announced in 2029 without an admission of causation.

safety_ledger.effect: Lean mass (muscle) loss and bone-density loss
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Follow-up Medicare analyses hold the hip-fracture HR at ~1.25–1.35 for users 65+ after 2 years. About 40% of users 65+ had a DXA scan in 2029. Cyclers and older women remain most at risk. Some geriatric practices now taper users over 75 off the drug.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class warning (2028) retained. CMS DXA code in use. The tirzepatide dementia PA requires documented bone assessment.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Conflicting cohorts; absolute risk very low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Listed in adverse reactions; no class warning.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No new signal, including in the AUD and gambling-disorder trials.

FICTIONAL: The FDA-requested postmarketing cohort (n≈61k, validated SHAPS scale) plus pooled trial reanalysis found clinically meaningful anhedonia in ~6.8% of users vs ~3.1% of matched non-users. It is dose-related, higher with tirzepatide at top doses (~8.5%), and reverses partly within 4–8 weeks of dose reduction. Milder 'evenness' is reported by about a quarter of users.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled in Oct 2029 under Warnings and Precautions as 'anhedonia and emotional blunting', with the prevalence estimate, advice to reassess dose, and a patient medication guide. The same reward mechanism is cited as the rationale in the 2030 addiction-disorders label.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Half to two-thirds regain within 18 months, worse after repeated cycles. The fat-over-muscle regain pattern is confirmed.
More case series, concentrated in gray-market and microdosing users outside clinical care.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: In professional guidance; no label change.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects (>5 years), adolescents, repeated cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About eight years of follow-up exist. The first interim pediatric bone-density data (2030) show slower BMD accrual in a small adolescent cohort; the result is not conclusive.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Pediatric BMD postmarketing requirement ongoing; AAP issued 2030 guidance favouring annual DXA for adolescents on long-term therapy.

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit / imported product harms (dosing errors, contamination, mislabelled contents)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: ~19,000 cumulative FDA reports tied to non-approved product by mid-2030. The Aug 2029 counterfeit 'tirzepatide' pens containing insulin caused a hypoglycaemia cluster of 212 hospitalisations and 9 deaths across 14 states. Poison-centre calls are up ~6× since 2025, mostly mg/unit errors, and pediatric accidental exposures are rising.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Expanded import alert. CBP mail seizures up ~4×. FDA 'verified pharmacy' labelling campaign. Lawsuits by states against marketplaces and payment processors. Personal importation is still not effectively policed.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Holiday-season and post-vacation ER spikes in vomiting, dehydration and acute kidney injury among users who restart at full dose.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Covered by the 2029 re-titration label language; CDC holiday advisory.

food_and_beverage.state: About 38% of households now have a user. Snack and confectionery volumes are down ~8–9% from 2025 and sugary drinks ~8%. Dollar sales are roughly flat to slightly down because price increases are reaching a ceiling. Hershey and Mondelez closed two US plants between them. Protein and fibre lines keep growing. Discount grocers report the first volume dips in lower-income zip codes as gray-market use spreads there.

alcohol.state: Spirits volumes are down ~11% from 2025 and beer ~7%. The AUD label lets employers and EAPs prescribe on-label. Craft distilleries are consolidating, and Brown-Forman shut another Kentucky facility. Non-alcoholic sales keep growing but replace only a fraction of the lost volume.

restaurants.state: Traffic is flat and average check slightly down. Small plates are standard. Casino buffets in Las Vegas and Atlantic City are mostly gone, and late-night bar hours in mid-sized cities keep shrinking. 'Off-night' dinner events tied to drug holidays have become a weekend niche.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists keep shrinking. Stretch and adjustable-waist lines dominate mainstream racks, and clothing rental for cyclers is growing modestly.

fitness.state: Strength gyms, DXA chains and employer 'metabolic track' gym check-ins keep growing. Police and military fitness contracts are a new B2B line.

insurance.state: Employer coverage is flat at 43%. Pharmacy trend fell to ~+6% as net prices declined. Adherence-verified tracks cover ~4M employees. After the anhedonia label, plans must offer a dose-reduction 'reasonable alternative' without losing the premium differential, which PBMs now administer. Medicare's dementia-route spending is ~$5B a year.

pharma.state: Lilly and Novo still dominate. US net prices are declining slowly and volumes rising. The addiction-disorder label opens a psychiatry channel for Novo. Brand-protection and anti-counterfeit spending is now a reported line in annual reports. Indian and Chinese generic exporters grow fastest.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Thin no longer distinguishes anyone; how a body got thin does. A lean body with muscle reads as branded pill plus trainer. A lean, slightly gaunt one in a working-class job reads as 'mail-order'. A body visibly heavier after the holidays reads as someone who took a holiday.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Prevalence has converged: the bottom third is up to 19% because of cheap vials. The quality gap has widened. The insured get DXA, dose reviews and anhedonia screening; the gray-market tier gets uncertain strength and the poison-centre number.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: 'Off weekends' have become a social form: some families plan Sunday dinners and Thanksgiving around a skipped dose and accept the GI cost of restarting. The Tulsa-born 'Bread Alone' fasting network claims ~900 congregations across the South and Midwest.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Apps added 'on / off / holiday' status. 'Holiday partner' is slang for a relationship that mostly lives in drug-free weekends.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: After the label put joylessness in writing, the counter-movement got a document to wave. Fat-acceptance revivalists, MAHA-aligned 'natural appetite' influencers, church fasting groups and the Unmuted collective (now with chapters in Detroit and Oakland) hold joint 'Feel It' rallies without agreeing on any platform. The mainstream reading has shifted from appetite as noise to appetite as something you dose.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Labelled in Oct 2029 at ~6.8% vs ~3.1% for clinically meaningful anhedonia. About a quarter of users report milder flattening. Surveys suggest ~35% of current users deliberately skip or reduce doses at least monthly to 'get feeling back', and dose-down to the lowest effective maintenance dose is now routine clinical advice.
interior_life.framing: Mostly a side effect, sometimes a treatment. The same mechanism is a labelled adverse effect on one page of the leaflet and the rationale for the gambling-disorder indication on another. Employers have stopped saying 'steadiness' in public materials. Users talk about 'the flat', 'the blanket' and 'off weekends'.
interior_life.effect_on_work: About 4M employees are in adherence-verified tracks, and the labelled dose-reduction alternative now preserves the premium. EEOC settled one of the two ADA charges in 2029; the other is in litigation. Shift-work employers (warehousing, trucking, hospitals) still favour adherent staff for night rotations. Since the label, 'blunted' is a reason given in performance reviews and grievance hearings.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: Sportsbook handle growth has stalled in states with high incretin use. Operators court the off-weekend crowd with Friday promotions, and Nevada regulators are studying 'holiday surge' betting patterns. 'Flat' fiction has peaked and an 'off-night' music scene of loud, short sets has replaced it. Telehealth clinics market compulsive-shopping and screen-time scripts to parents and young adults.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Desire mismatch is the standard couples-therapy complaint. Planned drug holidays around anniversaries, vacations and conception attempts are common, and so are holiday-restart ER visits.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The anhedonia label armed a cross-ideological coalition. California banned adherence-conditioned premiums in Jan 2030, joining Illinois, and three other states are debating bills. Libertarian and labour voices object to the military and police readiness programmes. There is no measurable effect on turnout. Gambling-industry lobbyists quietly oppose any mandate-like use.

state.regulatory_posture: Approvals move quickly on new indications for existing products (the addiction-disorders label) but the agency is cautious on new molecules (retatrutide CRL, survodutide delay). It labelled anhedonia once the postmarketing data came in. Enforcement against imports is tough in rhetoric and porous in practice.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: No mandate and no structural coverage change. TrumpRx managed price cuts in Jan 2029. The 30% wellness differential guidance stands, amended in 2029 to require a dose-reduction alternative after the anhedonia label.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: PBM fill data and app-linked logs still feed wellness vendors. The DoD readiness programme logs supervised dosing in unit medical records. Two Medicaid programmes still condition coverage on adherence and BMI. Police departments in Phoenix, Houston and Jacksonville offer incretin coverage tied to fitness-test standards.
state.workforce_or_military: Since Jun 2029 the DoD Metabolic Readiness Program has offered supervised oral semaglutide to active-duty personnel who fail the body-composition standard or are at risk of separation. About 140k service members are enrolled, with drug supplied through military treatment facilities, and it is extended to recruits within 10% of the weight standard. The Air Force bars it in flight crews for 4 weeks during titration. The FAA permits stable-dose use for pilots with an AME report. DOT issued guidance in 2030 allowing truckers to use incretins for AUD on a stable dose. Union-negotiated programmes cover nurses' and firefighters' shift workers.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: India and China supply most global incretin volume. The US–India trade framework includes a mail-enforcement annex with little effect. US prices still run ~10–30× Indian generic prices after managed cuts. A Pentagon supply review flagged dependence on Danish and US API capacity for the readiness programme.

events.event: TrumpRx and manufacturers announce second-round cash prices: Wegovy pill and Foundayo maintenance doses fall to $199–249 a month and injectables to $249–349; starting doses stay at $149, and PBMs report ~12% lower net commercial prices
Pentagon launches Metabolic Readiness Program offering supervised oral semaglutide to service members failing body-composition standards; ~140,000 enrolled within a year

CDC and FDA trace counterfeit 'tirzepatide' pens filled with insulin to 212 hospitalisations and 9 deaths across 14 states; gray-market users estimated at 9 million as poison-centre calls hit six times 2025 levels
FDA adds anhedonia and emotional blunting to the warnings for all incretins, citing ~6.8% of users versus ~3.1% of non-users, and tells prescribers to reassess the dose

California bans premium differentials tied to GLP-1 adherence after a campaign by fat-acceptance groups, unions, MAHA legislators and church fasting networks; 'Feel It' rallies draw crowds in Los Angeles and Detroit

FDA approves oral semaglutide for alcohol use disorder and gambling disorder, the first incretin label for a compulsive behaviour; telehealth off-label scripts for shopping and screen compulsion surge

open_tensions: The same reward-dampening mechanism is a labelled harm and a labelled treatment. Users self-titrate between joy and control with drug holidays that cause restart injuries, while employers and the military still reward continuous dosing.

Nine million Americans take mail-order product because brand prices fell only to $149–349. After the insulin-counterfeit deaths enforcement is still losing to the mail, and generic exclusivity ends around 2031–32.
Medicare pays ~$5B a year for a contested dementia benefit in exactly the age group carrying the bone warning, and a confirmatory trial is due before anyone resolves it.
Upper-income adolescents and a growing gray-market youth fringe are medicated through peak-bone-mass years. The first interim pediatric BMD data are worrying but inconclusive.

prose.headline: Sixty-Five Million on It, Nine Million on the Mail, and a Label That Finally Says the Quiet Part: It Can Take Your Joy
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2030 about one American adult in four is taking an incretin drug, and almost one in three has tried one. For most new users that means a daily pill. The government's cash channel still sells starting doses for $149. Since a price round in January 2029, maintenance doses cost $199 to $249, which is cheaper but still not cheap. Wegovy's list price of $1,349 is still printed on boxes nobody pays for. Who pays has not changed. Fewer than half of employers cover the drugs for weight loss, Medicare pays only through disease codes, and Medicaid depends on which state you live in.

The growth came from somewhere else. Roughly nine million people now take generic semaglutide mailed from India, or vials of Chinese tirzepatide sold as research chemicals, or pens that are not what they claim to be. In August 2029 counterfeit tirzepatide pens turned out to contain insulin, and 212 people across fourteen states were hospitalised with collapsing blood sugar. Nine died. Poison centres take six times as many calls as in 2025, mostly about milligrams confused with units. The packages kept coming. For the bottom third of earners the drugs became nearly as common as for everyone else, but without the scans, the dose reviews or the certainty about what is in the vial.

In October 2029 the FDA put in writing what users had been saying for years. Every incretin label now warns of anhedonia and emotional blunting and gives the numbers: about seven in a hundred users against three in a hundred non-users, worse at the top doses and partly reversible on a lower one. Six months later the agency approved oral semaglutide for alcohol use disorder and gambling disorder on the same mechanism. The leaflet now describes the drug's effect on reward as a harm on one page and a treatment on another. Telehealth clinics have started prescribing it for compulsive shopping and teenagers' screen time.

What used to be a niche side effect is now an everyday complaint, and people manage it themselves. About a third of users skip or cut doses at least monthly to feel things again. Families plan Sunday dinners around a skipped pill. Emergency rooms see a spike after every holiday, when people restart at full dose and spend the night vomiting. The FDA has added re-titration instructions to the labels.

Employers have stopped saying 'steadiness' in public, but the programmes continue. About four million workers are in adherence-verified metabolic tracks, which since the label must accept a lower dose as compliance. The Pentagon now treats the pill as readiness infrastructure. About 140,000 service members who failed body-composition standards take supervised oral semaglutide rather than face separation. Police departments in Phoenix and Houston tie coverage to fitness tests, and the DOT has cleared truckers on stable doses for alcohol treatment.

The backlash got a document to cite. Fat-acceptance revivalists, union locals, MAHA-aligned legislators, Southern church fasting networks and the Unmuted artists, who now have chapters in Detroit and Oakland, share stages at 'Feel It' rallies and agree on nothing but the label. In January they got California to ban adherence-conditioned premiums.

The new drugs didn't arrive. Retatrutide got a rejection letter, and survodutide is sold in Europe but not yet in the US. Older users are still caught between a contested dementia benefit Medicare now pays about $5 billion a year for and a bone warning that says their hips are paying too. Teenagers on the drugs are going through their bone-building years, and the first data on that are worrying and inconclusive. Snack volumes fell again, spirits again, casino buffets are mostly gone. From the outside the country looks thinner, soberer and calmer. Inside, many people have learned to take off the edge of their pleasure on weekdays and put it back on weekends.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Tess Lindqvist, fifty-one, deals blackjack on the swing shift at a casino in Reno. The pill sits on her nightstand beside a glass of water: Wegovy, 25 milligrams, covered by the union plan once the casino's doctor wrote 'sleep apnoea' on the form. She takes it Monday through Friday. Saturdays she doesn't.

The pit boss calls her steady. Players call her cold, and some of them tip less for it. She deals eleven hands a minute and feels nothing when a man in a Raiders cap pushes his whole stack in and loses it. He tells her he's on the new one for gambling. She says, 'Good luck with that,' and she means it, mildly.

On break she reads the leaflet again, the part that says anhedonia. The pharmacist circled it. Seven in a hundred. She doesn't know if she's one of the seven or just tired.

Her brother Dale texts a photo of a vial from Hyderabad that cost him thirty-one dollars. Is this 2.5 milligrams or 2.5 units, he asks. She sends him the poison-control number and a heart.

At three a.m. she drives home past the old buffet, which is a pickleball hall now. Saturday she skips the pill. By evening she is hungry the way she was at twenty. She makes her mother's cardamom buns, eats two, cries at a dog-food commercial, and laughs at herself for crying.

Sunday night she takes the pill again, half-dose, the way the label says, and lies awake waiting for the flat to come back.
